title: Station effects reduced the report-signal contrast in six mixed-report Hawaii tsunami events
abstract: We test station selection in a fixed Hawaii tsunami sample with 22 earthquakes and six stations in 2015-2026. There are 132 complete six-minute water-level windows and 31 matched NCEI reports. The event-only ratio of short-period signal at reported versus other windows is 2.26. Adding station intercepts reduces it to 1.17 (95% event-bootstrap interval 0.89-1.56). The log contrast falls by 81%, a model comparison rather than a causal fraction. Only six events have mixed station report status. An exact conditional test fixes event and station report totals and enumerates all 328 feasible report tables. Its primary two-sided p value is 0.079. Alternative signal indices also have intervals that include one. Thus extra station-level signal selection remains unresolved after harbour controls. This does not refute the earlier regional event-level wave-growth result. The exact tool removes additive event and station reporting effects under an independent Bernoulli model; joint reporting decisions can violate it. Six-minute signals are not tsunami peak heights. Six mixed events, one dense region, inherited selection and stable-station assumptions limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes and reproduction instructions are included. External source records remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Signal ratios after event and station controls. Intervals include one for all tested indices. Raw signal medians are shown at right.
